evidence: Plin. NH 32.108: ligna squatinae piscis cute (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The ordinary word for smoothing wood, stone, or a wall; Pliny has wood smoothed with the skin of the angel shark, the ancient sandpaper.

evidence: Varr. RR 3.11.3: omnēs parietēs tēctōriō lēvigantur (Lewis & Short)
Col. 8.15.2: ea tōta māceriēs opere tēctōriō lēvigātur
terms.comment: From lēvis, smooth (long e); not in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Polī tabulam, nē assulae digitōs pungant.
phrases.english: Sand the board down, so the splinters don’t prick your fingers.

phrases.latin: Sed ea tōta māceriēs opere tēctōriō lēvigātur extrā intrāque
phrases.english: But the whole wall is smoothed with plaster outside and in

phrases.latin: Cui dōnō lepidum novum libellum āridā modo pūmice expolītum?
phrases.english: To whom shall I give my charming new little book, just smoothed off with dry pumice?
